input.context: GEPA capture (FEAT-210) turns on for a second low-stakes agent this slice, after fullstack-dev-only S2 scope. The file-backed trial store (fileStore, one JSONL file per agent under .claude/artifacts/crew/gepa/trials/) has no retention policy — every real dispatch artifact write appends a trial row, forever. Plan for the point where capture is horizontalized to most builder agents (S5c) and trial volume grows from near-zero to potentially thousands of rows per agent per month.
constraints: Storage backend is pluggable (file | astramem per GepaConfigSchema) — the plan must work for the file backend today and not foreclose an astramem migration later
No trial row may ever be silently dropped without an audit trail (crew:gepa-invalidate already provides soft-delete, not hard deletion)
Retention/rotation must not race a concurrent captureTee write — file store already uses a walltime-guarded Promise.race

expected_output.summary: Cap active trial file size with a rotation policy (e.g. rotate to trials/<agent>/<agent>-<yyyymm>.jsonl once a threshold is hit) plus a documented external cold-storage/aggregation job that runs outside the write-hot-path; fileStore.put() itself stays a simple append, rotation is a separate maintenance script (crew:prune-artifacts sibling) run on a schedule, not inline in captureTee
expected_output.non_goals_explicit: Does not implement compaction/aggregation logic in this design — only the rotation boundary and where a future job would hook in; does not change the astramem backend contract
failure_modes_named: Rotation script racing an in-flight captureTee write on the same file — mitigated by rotation touching only files older than the current month, never the active file
Unbounded growth if the rotation script itself is never scheduled — needs an explicit cron/hook owner named in the follow-up FEAT, not left implicit

dependencies_graphed.file_store: gepa-core fileStore(root).put() — unchanged, still a simple append
dependencies_graphed.rotation_script: new scripts/lib/gepa/rotate-trials.ts — moves closed-month files, never touches current-month file
dependencies_graphed.scheduling: cron-equivalent or crew:prune-artifacts sibling command; scheduling owner is an open question for the follow-up FEAT

interfaces_typed.RotationBoundary: { agent: string; activeMonth: string; rotateBefore: string }

expected_output.test_strategy_present: Unit: rotation script given a fixture directory with 3 months of files rotates the 2 older ones and leaves the current-month file untouched; integration: concurrent captureTee write during a rotation run does not corrupt either file (walltime race already covers write-side; rotation adds a read-only listing pass first)
expected_output.tradeoffs_articulated: In-band rotation inside captureTee (check size on every write) was rejected — it adds latency to the write-hot-path that must stay under the walltime budget; out-of-band scheduled rotation costs eventual-consistency (file can exceed the target size between runs) but keeps captureTee simple and fast

notes: hand-seed 2026-07-02 FEAT-210 — held-out set expansion for detectEvalDrift minSampleSize; capacity_planning scenario, not previously represented in architect seeds.
